prompt.brief: Design a predictive autoscaling system that forecasts service demand, combines predictions with safety limits and current capacity, and proactively scales infrastructure without causing oscillation or runaway cost.
successSignals: Separate observed metrics, forecasts, scaling policy, capacity reservations, actuator commands, and resulting health signals.
Forecast multiple horizons with confidence bands, combine prediction with reactive safeguards, and smooth actions with cooldowns.
Coordinate dependent services in an order that preserves capacity and avoid scaling on corrupted, delayed, or feedback-loop data.
Explain cold start, event-driven spikes, model drift, quota failure, rollback, cost budgets, and manual override.

functional: Collect service metrics and calendars, produce forecasts, evaluate confidence, and calculate a bounded desired capacity.
Apply scale-up and scale-down actions across dependent services with approvals, cooldowns, health checks, and audit history.
Expose forecast, recommendation, actual capacity, action result, cost, model version, and manual override state.
nonFunctional: Target demand forecast error within 15% on declared workloads while reactive utilization limits protect the SLO.
Scale decisions for thousands of services with dependency-aware queues and per-service rate and cost limits.
Make forecast publication and actuator commands idempotent and require observed state before repeating a scale action.
Fall back to reactive autoscaling and safe capacity floors when forecasts, metrics, or provider APIs fail.
scaleAssumptions: Manage 10,000 services across regions with minute-level signals and burst events such as launches or campaigns.
Partition forecasts by service, region, and horizon; isolate noisy services and coordinated dependency groups.
Retain metrics, feature cutoffs, forecasts, actions, policy versions, outcomes, and cost evidence for replay.

metrics.description: Keep Use time-series forecasting (Prophet, DeepAR) for demand prediction, Implement multi-step forecasting for different horizons, Use calendar features for event-driven scaling off the synchronous path.

architecture.title: Predictive Auto Scaling System ML platform architecture
architecture.summary: Design a predictive autoscaling system that forecasts service demand, combines predictions with safety limits and current capacity, and proactively scales infrastructure without causing oscillation or runaway cost. The design separates reproducible data and feature lineage from queued training, approved model promotion, version-pinned serving, and feedback-driven monitoring.

deepDives.title: Reproducibility and leakage prevention
points: Pin predictive auto scaling system data, feature, code, dependency, and model versions for every run.
Use point-in-time joins and quarantine failed quality or privacy checks before training.
Keep raw inputs and artifacts immutable so a result can be replayed after a dependency changes.

deepDives.title: Safe promotion and serving contracts
points: Separate predictive auto scaling system model registration from deployment and require signed artifacts plus schema compatibility.
Use shadow traffic, canaries, rollback pointers, and per-version latency/error budgets.
Return model version and feature freshness so clients can explain or reproduce a prediction.

deepDives.title: Drift, feedback, and cost
points: Measure feature drift, prediction drift, label delay, and segment-level quality for predictive auto scaling system rather than only aggregate accuracy.
Sample expensive inference and cap retraining concurrency with an explicit GPU or compute budget.
Keep human corrections and delayed labels linked to the original prediction and model version.

tradeoffs.title: Batch versus online features
tradeoffs.recommendation: Prefer a shared feature contract with batch backfills and a low-latency online serving path for decisions that need freshness.
tradeoffs.caution: Two independently defined transformations create training-serving skew and hard-to-debug regressions.

tradeoffs.title: Synchronous versus asynchronous inference
tradeoffs.recommendation: Keep interactive predictive auto scaling system inference synchronous within a strict budget and queue large or expensive jobs.
tradeoffs.caution: A request path that waits for model loading, enrichment, or retraining turns downstream slowness into an outage.

tradeoffs.title: Global model versus segment models
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with one versioned model and add segment-specific models only when quality or policy evidence justifies the operational cost.
tradeoffs.caution: Many simultaneously active versions multiply monitoring, rollback, and data-lineage burden.

commonMistakes: Training predictive auto scaling system on mutable data without recording a replayable dataset version.
Serving features from a different transformation or time window than the training job used.
Promoting a model on one offline metric without canary, safety, or segment-level checks.
Treating delayed labels and drift as a dashboard concern instead of a retraining input.
Allowing retries to create duplicate runs, artifacts, or promotions without idempotency keys.

followUps.question: How do you roll back a bad predictive auto scaling system model?
followUps.answer: Keep immutable artifacts and a last-known-good pointer; switch traffic atomically, stop promotion, and preserve affected prediction traces for analysis.

followUps.question: How do you detect training-serving skew?
followUps.answer: Compare feature definitions and sampled values by entity and event time, expose source watermarks, and alert on divergence before quality drops.

followUps.question: What happens when labels arrive weeks later?
followUps.answer: Store prediction records with model and feature versions, join delayed labels idempotently, and compute drift or quality by cohort.
